prevalent

/PREV-uh-luhnt/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Prevalent means existing or occurring frequently in a particular place or at a particular time.

Smartphones are so prevalent among teenagers that a classroom without them feels strange.

Example

Before vaccines existed, measles was prevalent in nearly every town, infecting most children before age ten.

Measles wasn't just present — it occurred frequently, almost everywhere, at that time. Prevalent describes exactly that pattern: commonly found throughout a place or period.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

widespread: Widespread means extending over a large area or reaching many people — widespread damage, widespread support. It measures sheer extent. Prevalent measures frequency within a setting: how commonly a condition, practice, or belief turns up in a particular place or group. Flood damage is widespread across a region; a belief is prevalent among its people.

pervasive: Pervasive describes something that has soaked into every part of a thing — a pervasive smell, a pervasive mood of distrust — usually an intangible working its way through. Prevalent is about how often something is found across a group or place, not how deeply it saturates any one thing.

rife: Rife means teeming with something bad, and it sits after what it describes — an industry rife with fraud, a town rife with rumors. Prevalent is neutral and takes normal adjective positions: smartphones or beliefs can be prevalent with no judgment and no special word order attached.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

rare: seldom found or occurring

scarce: existing in amounts too small to meet demand

Where it sits · how widely it is found — common → prevalent → ubiquitous

common vs. prevalent: Common is weaker — it just means something happens often; prevalent adds the sense that it dominates a particular place or time.

ubiquitous vs. prevalent: Ubiquitous is stronger — it claims something is found absolutely everywhere at once, while prevalent means widespread within a specific setting.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — pre-

Prefix — pre-: before, in advance (Latin prae-)

Root — val

Root — val: to be strong, to have power (Latin valere)

Suffix — -ent

Suffix — -ent: in a state of; -ing (adjective ending)

Put it together

Put it together: Pre- ('before, ahead of') + valere ('to be strong') builds Latin praevalere — 'to be stronger than the rest, to win out.' What is prevalent has out-muscled the alternatives, strength 'ahead of' everything else, and now shows up everywhere in that place or time.

Use the root in a new word: valor

Use the root in a new word: valor: The firefighter received a medal for valor after carrying two children from the burning building.

Strength Check

Word Choice

Formal / academic

Prevalent usually takes 'in' or 'among' ('prevalent in cities,' 'prevalent among voters') and describes conditions, practices, beliefs, or diseases that occur frequently across a group or place. It describes how often something is found — not how physically large one instance of it is.
